title: Efficient Multiscale Simplicial Complex Generation for Mapper
subtitle: Funding: Air Force Research Labs
abstract: The primary result of the Mapper framework is the geometric realization of a simplicial complex, depicting topological relationships and structures suitable for visualizing, analyzing, and comparing high dimensional data. As an unsupervised tool, Mapper naturally relies on parameters that control the relational component of the output complex; this project introduces new algorithms to efficiently march through successive Mapper realizations and make them stable and tractable.

title: Bringing High Performance Density-based Clustering to R
subtitle: Funding: Air Force Research Labs
abstract: Density-based clustering techniques are popular because they can recover non-convex, natural groups, but scalable implementations are scarce. This project delivers fast, state-of-the-art density-based algorithms in R, along with companion tools that make these methods accessible for computationally difficult problems.

title: Automating Point of Interest Discovery in Geospatial Contexts
subtitle: Semi-supervised density level set estimation
abstract: A semi-supervised framework for automating point-of-interest discovery that balances heuristic detection methods with density-based estimation guarantees, enabling flexible incorporation of labeled information while scaling to large geospatial data sets.

title: Spectral Relaxations of Persistent Rank Invariants
subtitle: Spectral families and efficient approximation
abstract: A framework for continuous relaxations of the persistent rank invariant that retain stability, incorporate Laplacian structure, and admit randomized algorithms for efficient approximation. We explore applications in parameter optimization and shape classification.

title: Move Schedules: Fast persistence computations in coarse dynamic settings
subtitle: Funding: Ginther Fellowship & NSF CCF-2006661
abstract: Coarsening the maintenance of boundary decompositions across filtrations allows sublinear storage and faster persistence computations for dynamic data by reducing the number of state transitions when the filtration ordering shifts.

title: Towards Autonomous Aerial Refueling: Massive Parallel Iterative Closest Point
subtitle: Funding: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
abstract: We expose the intrinsic parallelism of iterative closest point by combining a logarithmic approximate search with a rapid Delaunay Traversal, delivering vectorized searches that beat brute-force and branch-and-bound baselines for real-time autonomy.
